rows.grounds: instrumental of sāmarasya (perfect fusion) + ātman; describes the mode of operation
feminine demonstrative referring back to the previously described power
instrumental abstract noun indicating reversal or inward return

items.question: By what mode of perfect fusion and turning back does this power operate on all sides?
premises: This same power is the subject of operation.
Perfect fusion constitutes its essential mode.
Turning back occurs on all sides.
items.inference: Therefore this power operates pervasively through a turning back characterized by perfect fusion.
items.plain_english: By the nature of perfect fusion, this same power, through turning back, operates on all sides.

rows.grounds: compound: viṣaya-ābhoga (sense-object enjoyment) + sambhūta (arisen) + camatkāra (wonder) + upabṛṃhita (augmented)

items.question: What quality intensifies the experience arising from the enjoyment of sense objects?
premises: Enjoyment of sense objects takes place.
This wonder serves to augment the experience.
items.inference: Therefore the experience is intensified by wonder born from sense enjoyment.
items.plain_english: It is augmented by the wonder that arises from the enjoyment of sense objects.

rows.grounds: instrumental of bīja-bhāva (seed state) + ātman; describes the union's latent mode
melāpa/mela, the confluence or assembly central to the Krama context
adjective qualifying the union, suggesting cohesion or fluid intimacy
relative pronoun introducing the characterization of the union
instrumental of pratyag-ātman (inward self); indicates inward orientation

items.question: What characterizes the moist union that exists in the seed state and as the inward self?
premises: A union exists as the subject.
This union has the nature of a seed state.
This union is moist and has the nature of the inward self.
items.inference: Therefore the union is characterized as a moist, inwardly oriented presence in seed form.
items.plain_english: The union which, by the nature of the seed state and by the nature of the inward self, is moist.
